$comment: Illustrative cost model for the pipeline explorer. Numbers are a model of two designs, not production measurements. The document profile is a public IETF RFC; the pipeline is described at pattern level only.

document.title: RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics (sections 8–15 profile)
document.note: A public IETF standard stands in for an engineering specification: same shape — numbered normative clauses (MUST / SHOULD / MAY), cross-references to other standards, and pages that are pure table of contents or boilerplate.

stages.name: Classify document
stages.summary: One cheap call decides what kind of document arrived: a requirements spec, a standards list, a diagram, or a reference document. Everything downstream branches on that answer.
stages.why: A spec and a norms catalogue need opposite treatment. Guessing wrong wastes every later call, so the decision is made first, once, and cheaply.
stages.guards: Per-customer document conventions are looked up rather than inferred, so a recurring house format never gets re-guessed.

stages.name: Page triage
stages.summary: Decide which pages carry requirements at all. Tables of contents, title pages, approval sheets and blank pages are dropped before anything expensive runs.
stages.why: About a third of a typical document is not extractable. Skipping it is the cheapest optimisation in the whole pipeline.
stages.guards: The triage result also sets an expected requirement count per page, which the recall guard uses later to notice under-extraction.

stages.name: Extract requirements
stages.summary: One strong call per extractable page, the page image as primary input and the markdown text as context. Pages run concurrently, not serially.
stages.why: Layout carries meaning in engineering documents — tables, indents, numbered clauses. Text-only extraction lost it; vision-first extraction keeps it.
stages.guards: Page metadata (drawing refs, page numbers) is fenced with explicit do-not-extract markers so it cannot become a ghost requirement. A recall guard retries any page whose yield is far below the triage estimate.

stages.name: Standards-code scan
stages.summary: Find every referenced standard (ISO 8601, RFC 5234, …), normalise the spelling, expand ranges, merge duplicates across pages. Deterministic code does the work; a cheap model call filters false positives at the end.
stages.why: The first version asked the model to list codes page by page. It missed some, invented others, and formatted the same code four ways. A prefix-agnostic scanner is exhaustive and deterministic; the model is only asked the one question it is good at — is this really a standard?
stages.guards: Canonicalisation and cross-page merge happen before the model sees anything, so it cannot re-introduce duplicates.

stages.name: Enrich requirements
stages.summary: Category, criticality, owning team and a first feasibility opinion for each requirement — all four fields from one batched call over ten to fifteen requirements at a time.
stages.why: Four separate per-requirement stages meant four system prompts, four round-trips and four chances to time out for every single clause. One batched call sees neighbouring requirements too, which improves consistency of the labels.
stages.guards: Model output is parsed defensively at every site; a malformed batch is repaired or re-requested rather than dropped. Reviewer corrections from earlier projects are injected as hints behind a coverage gate.

stages.name: Feasibility from evidence
stages.summary: For each requirement, retrieve what past projects said about similar clauses, rank the evidence, then reason over a batch of ten with citation labels the model must use.
stages.why: Without retrieval the model answers from general knowledge and sounds confident about things nobody in the company has ever built. With retrieval and mandatory citations, every verdict points at something a human can open.
stages.guards: Claims without a citation to retrieved evidence are stripped and the batch is retried once. Near-identical past requirements with an explicit verdict short-circuit with no model call at all.

stages.name: Finalize
stages.summary: Rule-based de-duplication across files, one call to summarise the project goal, one to extract basic document metadata.
stages.why: De-duplication is a set operation; it never needed a model. Keeping it deterministic makes the output stable between runs.
stages.guards: Byte-identical re-uploads are recognised by content hash and reuse the previous result with zero calls.

stages.name: Translate output
stages.summary: Every requirement text into each target language. Batched twenty-five strings per call, cached in memory so repeated phrases translate once.
stages.why: Translating one string per call made this stage the slowest in the pipeline for a step that adds no intelligence.
stages.guards: Translation uses a cheap model with an explicit fallback chain; a failed batch retries item by item so one bad string cannot block a document.
